title: Comparing the areas under two or more correlated receiver operating characteristic curves: a nonparametric approach
harvard_reference: DeLong, E.R., DeLong, D.M. and Clarke-Pearson, D.L. (1988) 'Comparing the areas under two or more correlated receiver operating characteristic curves: a nonparametric approach', Biometrics, 44(3), pp. 837-845. doi:10.2307/2531595.
abstract_summary: The paper addresses how to compare diagnostic tests that produce a continuous or graded score, where each test is summarised by its ROC curve and the area beneath it. Its central point is that when two or more empirical ROC curves are built from tests applied to the same individuals, the resulting AUC estimates are correlated and any test of their difference must account for that correlation. The authors propose a nonparametric method that treats the AUC as a generalised U-statistic and derives an estimated covariance matrix for a set of correlated AUCs, from which differences can be tested.

claims_supported.claim: The DeLong test provides a nonparametric comparison of correlated ROC AUCs computed on the same cases.
claims_supported.where: Abstract (PubMed PMID 3203132): the paper states that when two or more empirical ROC curves are constructed from tests performed on the same individuals, analysis of differences must account for the correlated nature of the data, and that it presents a nonparametric approach to analysing areas under correlated ROC curves using generalised U-statistics theory to produce an estimated covariance matrix. This is exactly the nonparametric, same-cases, correlated-AUC comparison described in the claim.
